findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this reports 2 pages instead of 1 (and for 100 it reports 3 instead of 2), so showingLast stays false on the real last page and the Next action advances to an empty page. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for non-zero counts.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members
findings.body: members now always applies limit (default 50) and offset, but the public discourse/templates/group/members.hbs view and discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 route add no pagination controls or further fetching. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Groups with more than 50 members will now show only the first 50 on the public members page with no way to reach the rest.

findings.title: Group creation silently ignores the alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The client's Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible on POST /admin/groups, but create only assigns name and visible. A non-default alias level chosen in the admin form for a new group is silently discarded and the model default is used instead; update handles alias_level, so create should assign params[:alias_level] the same way.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded, zero or negative limit/offset
findings.body: limit and offset are taken from params with only to_i and no clamping. A request such as members.json?limit=1000000 forces serializing that many users in one response (memory/CPU/DoS risk), while limit=0 is echoed back in meta.limit and makes the admin client's totalPages/currentPage divide by zero, and negative values go straight into SQL limit/offset. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Remove-member link visibility checks `automatic` on the wrong context
findings.body: This template is rendered per member via {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so its context is the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property. {{#unless automatic}} therefore always renders the remove link, including for automatic groups whose members the server refuses to remove (422 from can_not_modify_automatic). The check needs the group's automatic flag, not the member's.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE members to groups#remove_member and the client issues DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route were broken or missing, and it is inconsistent with the sibling test at line 125 which correctly uses :delete. It should use xhr :delete.
